title: NumPy Normal and Uniform Distributions
learningObjectives: Explain the concepts behind numpy normal and uniform distributions.
Choose an appropriate NumPy random generator method and its parameters.
Use seeded generators for reproducible examples and tests.
Validate sample shape, range and data type.
Describe the assumptions and limitations of a finite random sample.

understand.concept: A probability distribution describes how random values are generated. The normal distribution is controlled by a mean and standard deviation. The uniform distribution assigns equal density across an interval. NumPy Generator methods return samples; they do not guarantee that a finite sample has an exact theoretical mean or frequency.
understand.whyItMatters: Normal and uniform models appear in measurement noise, simulation, randomized testing and introductory statistical modeling.
understand.analogy: A random generator is like a repeatable deck-shuffling machine: a starting seed and the sequence of operations determine the generated sequence.
understand.summary: A probability distribution describes how random values are generated. The normal distribution is controlled by a mean and standard deviation. The uniform distribution assigns equal density across an interval. NumPy Generator methods return samples; they do not guarantee that a finite sample has an exact theoretical mean or frequency.

explain.narrative: Run the examples and inspect the sample properties. A random sample is not a promise of exact theoretical frequencies; tests should focus on stable properties such as shape, valid range and reproducibility. examples.title: Sample from a normal distribution
examples.code:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
x = rng.normal(loc=0, scale=1, size=1000)
print(x.shape, bool(np.all((x > -5) & (x < 5))))
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates sample from a normal distribution with a seeded NumPy random generator so the validation is deterministic.

examples.title: Change the normal mean and scale
examples.code:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
x = rng.normal(loc=10, scale=2, size=500)
print(x.shape, bool(np.all(np.isfinite(x))))
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates change the normal mean and scale with a seeded NumPy random generator so the validation is deterministic.

examples.title: Sample from a uniform interval
examples.code:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
x = rng.uniform(low=4, high=9, size=100)
print(bool(np.all((x >= 4) & (x < 9))))
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates sample from a uniform interval with a seeded NumPy random generator so the validation is deterministic.

examples.title: Compare distribution sample sizes
examples.code:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(4)
a = rng.normal(size=25)
b = rng.uniform(size=40)
print(a.size, b.size)
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates compare distribution sample sizes with a seeded NumPy random generator so the validation is deterministic.

examples.title: Use a fixed generator in a test
examples.code:
import numpy as np
x = np.random.default_rng(8).uniform(-1, 1, size=20)
assert np.all((x >= -1) & (x < 1))
print('range checked')
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates use a fixed generator in a test with a seeded NumPy random generator so the validation is deterministic.

practise.guidedTask: Use a seeded NumPy Generator to create a sample relevant to numpy normal and uniform distributions. Print its shape and verify the model's required range or count constraints.
practise.independentTask: Write a small simulation using an appropriate distribution. Explain the model parameters, state the assumptions and add deterministic tests using a fixed seed.
hints: Prefer np.random.default_rng over the legacy global random state.
Use a fixed seed in lessons and tests, not necessarily in production simulations.
Check parameter constraints before generating samples.
Distinguish theoretical properties from observed sample statistics.
Use a larger sample only when it serves a clear statistical purpose.
practise.challenge: Compare two appropriate distributions with the same sample size, summarize their assumptions and create a reproducible validation routine.
validationCriteria: All five examples execute with the pinned NumPy version and match expected output.
A Generator is used rather than relying on global random state.
Tests check deterministic properties without claiming exact sample statistics.
The learner explains the model assumptions and limits.

questions.prompt: What does a seeded NumPy Generator provide?
questions.answer: A reproducible pseudo-random sequence when the generator and call sequence are the same.
options: A truly random sequence that can never repeat.
A reproducible pseudo-random sequence when the generator and call sequence are the same.
A guarantee of exact theoretical frequencies.
A generator that ignores its parameters.
questions.explanation: A seed initializes a deterministic pseudo-random process.

questions.prompt: Why should distribution parameters be chosen carefully?
questions.answer: They encode the assumptions and scale of the model.
options: They encode the assumptions and scale of the model.
They only change the printed format.
They guarantee a fixed sample mean.
They remove the need to validate data.
questions.explanation: Parameters define the distribution being modeled.

questions.prompt: Which check is generally robust for a generated sample?
questions.answer: Check its shape and valid range.
options: Require the sample mean to equal the theoretical mean exactly.
Check its shape and valid range.
Assume every generated value is unique.
Expect the same values from different seeds.
questions.explanation: Shape and support constraints are stable properties.

questions.prompt: What does sampling without replacement mean?
questions.answer: The same population item cannot be selected more than once in that sample.
options: The same population item cannot be selected more than once in that sample.
Every possible item must be selected.
The sample must be sorted.
The generator cannot use a seed.
questions.explanation: Without replacement, selected population members are not repeated.

questions.prompt: What is an important limitation of a finite random sample?
questions.answer: Observed frequencies and statistics can differ from theoretical values.
options: It always contains invalid values.
Observed frequencies and statistics can differ from theoretical values.
It cannot be reproduced with a seed.
It must have a normal distribution.
questions.explanation: Finite samples naturally vary around theoretical expectations.
